offence_severity: Life imprisonment or rigorous imprisonment for a term of not less than ten years, and fine
physical_harm: Injuries caused to the complainant with splinters from the pistol
number_of_offences: Two offences/counts charged, one finally upheld
premeditation_planning: The court found no premeditation or prearranged plan
key_evidence_accepted: The Court accepted that the accused appellant did not carry arms nor open fire, and that the main accused Khilai took out a pistol and pointed it at the complainant without any instigation from the accused appellant.
witness_credibility: The Court raised serious doubts about the truth and/or accuracy of the evidence of PW-3 (the complainant) and PW-4, particularly in view of the enmity and pre-existing family disputes between the parties.

legal_representation.accused: Saurabh Mishra and P. V. Yogeswaran, Advs.
legal_representation.state: Rahuk Kaushik, Ms. Bhuvneshwari Pathak, Ms. Shilpi Satyapriya Satyam and Rahul Khatri, Advs.

investigation_status: Chargesheet filed against the accused appellant and the main accused Khilai

appeal_history.trial_court: Convicted under Sections 307/34 of the Indian Penal Code
appeal_history.supreme_court: Allowed the appeal, acquitted the accused appellant

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused appellant instigated the main accused to kill the complainant, and that the main accused fired the pistol at the exhortation of the accused appellant, resulting in the complainant's injuries.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the prosecution failed to establish a pre-arranged common intention between the accused appellant and the main accused to kill the complainant, and that the main accused acted on his own initiative without any instigation from the accused appellant.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that common intention is necessary for joint liability under Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, and that pre-arranged intention must be established through proved facts and circumstances.
precedent_relied_upon: B.N. Srikantiah v. Siddiah AIR 1958 SC 672; Bharwad Mepa Dana and Anr. v. State of Bombay AIR 1960 SC 289; Harbans Kaur and Another v. State of Haryana (2005) 9 SCC 195; Manik Das & Ors. v. State of Assam AIR 2007 SC 2274; Abdul Mannan v. State of Assam (2010) 3 SCC 381; Lallan Rai & Ors. v. State of Bihar (2003) 1 SCC 268; Ashok Basho (2010) SCC 660; Barendra Kumar Ghosh AIR 1925 Privy Council 1
other_sentence_order: The accused appellant is acquitted and directed to be set free forthwith.
